messages:
leah: Hey folks — noticed console sparklines and heatmap widgets are stalling badly after yesterday's canary. Felt like ~300-700ms extra on first paint across many dashboards.

leah: Repro steps: open org usage dashboard, switch to 30d, pan across timeline. Charts hang, CPU spikes. Thought it was just my machine but telemetry and Sentry show many users.

tom: ugh. Which deploy?

leah: Canary ID 2026-03-18T16:12:00Z (deploy-bot posted). PR was #4125 (telemetry/client sampling changes + lazy-import refactor).

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-18T16:12:00Z -> eng-platform-canary. Commit: a6d9f3e. Monitored metrics: APDEX dropped 0.09, FCP +180ms on canary hosts.

arjun: do you have a flamegraph or profiler? Could be a new hot-path in telemetry client or prefetch change.

leah: quick perf trace attached (abbreviated):
```
Main thread:
  - parse chart bundle (120ms)
  - telemetry.init() (220ms)
  - render sparkline (300ms)
  - kv-prefetch queue stall (150ms)
```
Not the exact full trace but timeline shows telemetry.init crossing into render.

tom: telemetry.init shouldn't be sync on main. Did we accidentally change to sync init to register listeners early?

leah: there's a sync loop that waits for config in TelemetryClient.start() if window.__REDWOOD_PREFETCH is enabled. That flag toggled by the lazy-import refactor.

sasha: if it's waiting for prefetched config that could explain it. The prefetch code added a Promise.race with 500ms fallback which might be blocking other microtasks.

dave: I can repro on my MBP with throttled CPU. Looks like when the prefetch promise stalls, it holds up first paint for widgets that import telemetry before render.

arjun: Proposed quick mitigation: revert the telemetry sampling change or make telemetry.init async (defer to after first paint). Which is faster?

tom: revert is the fastest rollback path. But we can also ship a hotfix that changes TelemetryClient.start to schedule the heavy work via requestIdleCallback / setTimeout 0. That avoids rollback.

sasha: FYI this also ties into routing/quotas: telemetry now instruments per-route quota sampling synchronously; making that async will stop tokenized quota lookups from blocking.

leah: I'm +1 for patching to defer heavy work in telemetry and also triage the prefetch flag. If patch looks safe we can deploy a canary in an hour.

arjun: I'll open PR to wrap heavy init in `if (document.readyState === 'complete') scheduleImmediateInit(); else window.requestIdleCallback(init, {timeout: 200})` and remove synchronous waits. Reference: #4130.

leah: add a temporary feature-flag to disable prefetch affinity for consoles in the config service so we can toggle server-side without code rollout.

deploy-bot: Noted. Creating canary target group and tagging build.

dave: I'll run lighthouse + micro-profile on the canary once it's up. Also will add a quick metric in console telemetry to measure telemetry.init duration per session.

tom: Sounds good. Sasha, can you coordinate support messaging in case customers hit slowness?

sasha: Yep — I'll post a short note in #support and pin instructions for the workaround (switch to basic view) and we can mark canary rollout. :thumbsup:

leah: Thanks. If canary looks green by +30m we can roll forward; if not we'll revert. Tracking: #4130 (hotfix), #4125 (original), incident ticket INF-2026-03.

arjun: One more follow-up: after hotfix, we should audit any sync init paths in SDKs (embeddings, rerank) — they may have similar patterns. Adding to runbook.

leah: Agreed. Will create a short postmortem stub after we stabilize. Thanks all.
